title: What if Betelgeuse exploded tonight? 💥
subject: star
description:
Would you want to see it in your lifetime? 👇

What would happen if Betelgeuse went supernova? Simulations by UC Santa Barbara astronomers suggest the red giant in Orion would shine about as bright as a half Moon for over 3 months, stay visible in daylight for about a year and cast shadows at night. At about 700 light-years away, it's too far to harm Earth. Scientists expect the explosion within the next 100,000 years, not necessarily soon.

Sources: NASA Science ("What Is Betelgeuse? Inside the Strange, Volatile Star"), Astronomy magazine ("When Betelgeuse goes supernova, what will it look like from Earth?", simulations by J. Goldberg, E. Bauer and A. Howell, UC Santa Barbara)

scenes.text: If Betelgeuse exploded, you'd see a star in daylight.
It's the red giant on Orion's shoulder.
When it goes supernova, it will shine as bright as a half Moon for over 3 months.
It would cast shadows at night and hang in the blue sky for about a year.
But here's the strange part. Its light takes about 700 years to reach us, so the blast we'd see is centuries old.
Then it fades for good, and Orion loses its shoulder.
